newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Key events in Zaire's rebel war.
newsitem.headline: Key events in Zaire's rebel war.

text.p: Talks began in Cape Town on Thursday to bring together the Zaire government and its rebel enemies, who launched an armed campaign in October.
Here is a chronology of major events in the conflict leading up to the talks brokered by South African President Nelson Mandela.

-- Oct 7 - 1996 - Deputy governor of Zaire's South Kivu province tells 300,000-strong Banyamulenge community -- ethnic Tutsis settled in the region for generations -- to leave Zaire within a week or "be hunted down as rebels". Warning sparks a revolt.
-- Oct 24 - Rebels seize their first sizeable town, Uvira on the northern shore of Lake Tanganyika.
-- Oct 30 - Rebels capture Bukavu, capital of South Kivu province, amid scenes of slaughter. Bukavu's Roman Catholic archbishop is among the dead.
-- Nov 1 - Rebels backed by Rwandan soldiers gain control of Goma after battles in which about 500 people die.
-- Nov 2 - International aid workers flee Goma, leaving 1.1 million refugees in east Zaire without U.N. support or aid.
-- Nov 4 - President Mobutu Sese Seko, who has not been in Zaire since August, leaves Switzerland after cancer treatment for the French Riviera.
-- Nov 5 - Eight African countries hold summit in Nairobi, call for neutral military force to go to Zaire to help refugees.
-- Nov 9 - Security Council asks then U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali to lay the groundwork for a multinational force to help end the Zaire crisis.
-- Nov 12 - Canada offers to lead the international force to provide humanitarian aid.
-- Nov 13 - U.S. President Bill Clinton agrees in principle to order U.S. troops to participate "in limited fashion".
-- Nov 14 - Rebels bombard Mugunga, the biggest refugee camp, with rockets, mortars and heavy artillery for six hours.
-- Nov 15 - Thousands of frightened Rwandan refugees surge out of Mugunga and other camps and head for home. About half-a- million refugees eventually cross into Rwanda.
-- Nov 24 - Zaire marks 31 years of Mobutu's rule.

-- Nov 28 - General Maurice Baril, the Canadian commander of proposed U.N. force meets rebel leaders in Goma. Despite extensive tour of region, idea of U.N.-backed military intervention fizzles out after exodus of refugees.
-- Dec 5 - Ugandan troops patrol town of Kasese inside Zaire.
-- Dec 9 - Fleeing Zaire soldiers loot Maboya and other towns.
-- Dec 16 - Mandela and eight other African leaders meet in Kenya to discuss crisis in Central Africa, notably Zaire, but Kinshasa shuns the forum.
-- Dec 17 - Mobutu flies home to a rousing reception; appoints new armed forces chief and reshuffles government to plot counter-offensive. He returns to France three weeks later.
-- Dec 25 - Rebels say they took northeastern town of Bunia.
-- Jan 23 - Zaire says its promised counter-offensive is launched with recapture of Walikale by government troops.
-- Jan 30 - Rebels frustrate counter-attack; advance on several fronts, heading into mineral-producing Shaba Province.
-- Feb 5 - Kabila gives Mobutu Feb 21 deadline to relinquish power or face all-out rebel offensive.
-- Feb 17 - Zaire launches air offensive, bombing rebel-held towns of Bukavu, Shabunda and Walikale.

-- Feb 19 - U.N. envoy Mohammed Sahnoun ends talks in Kinshasa; Five African ministers meet in the Zaire capital to discuss the fighting; Mandela announces South Africa will host talks between rebel leaders and the Zaire government.
-- Feb 20 - Mandela's spokesman says talks started in Cape Town on bringing the warring parties together.
